_comment: Hands-free phrase matching, pinned once for both matchers:
* web/src/ui/composer/duplex.ts  isConfirmation / isExit (the live loop: the browser owns the microphone)
Matching is logic, so it exists in both languages. Its behaviour is shared as data instead:
duplex.test.ts and tests/test_voice_duplex.py run every case, so a rule changed on one side reds the other.
A case without `phrases` (or without one of its two lists) uses the shipped lists in
src/personalclaw/voice/phrases.json. `confirmation` and `exit` are what each matcher answers for `text`.
Keep both directions: the variants speech-to-text writes must match, and ordinary dictation must not.

cases.name: exit_written_as_one_word
cases.why: speech-to-text wrote a spoken 'Never mind.' as this

cases.name: exit_one_word_with_its_punctuation
cases.why: the same retraction with the full stop the transcript usually carries

cases.name: exit_hyphenated
cases.why: a hyphen only separates words

cases.name: exit_as_configured
cases.why: the phrase written the way it is configured

cases.name: exit_after_a_confirmation_in_the_same_chunk
cases.why: 'send it, never mind' must be heard as both, so the loop's exit-wins rule can discard it

cases.name: exit_with_its_apostrophe_dropped
cases.why: an apostrophe inside a word does not count

cases.name: exit_with_a_curly_apostrophe
cases.why: a typographic apostrophe is an apostrophe

cases.name: exit_phrase_word_said_as_two
cases.why: an exit may assemble one of its words from two: a missed exit can send, a false one only discards

cases.name: exit_phrase_configured_with_capitals_and_a_hyphen
cases.why: the configured phrase is folded the same way as the transcript

cases.name: exit_never_rewords
cases.why: folding drops separators and apostrophes, it never changes the words

cases.name: ordinary_word_containing_mind
cases.why: only whole words count
cases.text: Remind me to call the bakery about the order

cases.name: ordinary_word_containing_never
cases.why: only whole words count
cases.text: Whenever you can, check the timetable

cases.name: ordinary_mind
cases.why: one word of the phrase is not the phrase
cases.text: Mind the gap on the platform

cases.name: ordinary_never
cases.why: one word of the phrase is not the phrase

cases.name: ordinary_cancellation
cases.why: a longer word that begins with the phrase is not the phrase

cases.name: exit_folded_but_outside_the_tail
cases.why: folding does not widen the tail window: an idiom at the head of a long dictation is not a retraction
cases.text: Nevermind the weather, book the Tuesday ferry to the island for two

cases.name: confirmation_run_together
cases.why: a confirmation's words may run together

cases.name: confirmation_hyphenated
cases.why: a hyphen only separates words

cases.name: confirmation_with_a_curly_apostrophe
cases.why: a typographic apostrophe is an apostrophe

cases.name: confirmation_never_assembles_a_phrase_word
cases.why: a confirmation never builds one of its words from two that were said: a false confirmation sends

cases.name: confirmation_phrase_word_said_as_two
cases.why: the strict side of the asymmetry the exit case above relaxes

cases.name: confirmation_whole_words_only
cases.why: 'redo it' contains 'do it' but not at a word boundary

cases.name: confirmation_longer_word
cases.why: a longer word that begins with the phrase is not the phrase

cases.name: confirmation_outside_the_tail
cases.why: a confirmation at the head of a long dictation is part of the thought
cases.text: Go ahead and tell me what you think about the plan
